question.worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda ):$ $$ \begin{aligned}p(\lambda ) & =\text{det}(A-\lambda I) \\ & =|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda & -2 \\ 4 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| \\ & =(3-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )+8 \\ & ={\lambda }^{2}-1\end{aligned} $$ Now, let's divide $f(x)$ by $p(x)$ using long division:
$\,\,{x}^{20}$
${x}^{2}-1\,$ $\,\enclose{longdiv}{{x}^{22}\,-\,{x}^{20}\,+\,3x\,-\,2\phantom{|}}$
${x}^{22}$ $-$ ${x}^{20}$
$3x$ $-$ $2$
Therefore, we can write $f(x)$ as $$ \begin{aligned}f(x) & =q(x)p(x)+r(x) \\ & =q(x)p(x)+(3x-2)\end{aligned} $$ where $q(x)={x}^{20}.$ Replacing $x$ with $A,$ we have $$ f(A)=q(A)p(A)+(3A-2I). $$ According to the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we have $p(A)=O.$ Therefore, $$ \begin{aligned}f(A) & =q(A)p(A)+(3A-2I) \\ & =q(A)\cdot O+(3A-2I) \\ & =3A-2I \\ & =3[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\ & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 \\ 12 & -9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 \\ 12 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned} $$

feedback.worked_solution:
Let's start by finding the characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda ):$ $$ \begin{aligned}p(\lambda ) & =\text{det}(A-\lambda I) \\ & =|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda & -2 \\ 4 & -3-\lambda \end{aligned}| \\ & =(3-\lambda )(-3-\lambda )+8 \\ & ={\lambda }^{2}-1\end{aligned} $$ Now, let's divide $f(x)$ by $p(x)$ using long division:
$\,\,{x}^{20}$
${x}^{2}-1\,$ $\,\enclose{longdiv}{{x}^{22}\,-\,{x}^{20}\,+\,3x\,-\,2\phantom{|}}$
${x}^{22}$ $-$ ${x}^{20}$
$3x$ $-$ $2$
Therefore, we can write $f(x)$ as $$ \begin{aligned}f(x) & =q(x)p(x)+r(x) \\ & =q(x)p(x)+(3x-2)\end{aligned} $$ where $q(x)={x}^{20}.$ Replacing $x$ with $A,$ we have $$ f(A)=q(A)p(A)+(3A-2I). $$ According to the Cayley-Hamilton theorem, we have $p(A)=O.$ Therefore, $$ \begin{aligned}f(A) & =q(A)p(A)+(3A-2I) \\ & =q(A)\cdot O+(3A-2I) \\ & =3A-2I \\ & =3[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 4 & -3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\ & =[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 \\ 12 & -9\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\ & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -6 \\ 12 & -11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned} $$
